paperTitle: Deterministic Sub-Frame Web Animations for Headless Social Video Synthesis
authors: AJ Rahim et al. · Open Source Media Systems
coreClaim: Stepping the W3C Web Animations API frame-by-frame in headless Chromium eliminates real-time jitter and produces bit-identical MP4s.
problem: Real-time screen recording of browser animations suffers from frame drops, GPU scheduling variance, and non-deterministic timestamps in CI.
method: Pause all document.getAnimations() timelines and seek currentTime to exact (frameIndex / fps) * 1000ms ticks before piping raw PNG frames to FFmpeg.

results.detail: SHA-256 frame-hash identity across repeated 150-frame 30fps renders
Wall-clock render time for a 5-second 1080×1080 H.264 MP4 on consumer hardware
External network requests required when using bundled OFL WOFF2 fonts

takeaways: Decouple animation time from wall-clock time whenever rendering video in headless browsers.
Use CSS transforms and opacity with explicit duration tokens so every timeline is inspectable.
Validate text overflow and WCAG contrast before committing to a multi-second video encode.
